title: A clean settlement
visitorSees: One request creates a settlement. The steps list shows every row the engine wrote, in order, and the ledger entries and outbox events that came with it.

engineDoes.what: Looks up the idempotency key, creates the pending row, calls the gateway, finalizes.
One transaction: idempotency key (IN_PROGRESS), settlement PENDING, settlement.requested outbox event.
One transaction: status, DEBIT and CREDIT ledger entries, balances, settlement.confirmed outbox event, idempotency key COMPLETED.

lookFor: The key is written in the same transaction as the pending row. The ledger entries and the outbox event are written in the same transaction as the status change.
honestLimit: The external system is an in-memory mock. Nothing here proves behaviour against a real bank.

title: Retry with the same key (case 3: double delivery)
visitorSees: Re-sending the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored response. No second gateway call, no new rows, money moves once.

engineDoes.what: finds the key, sees COMPLETED, returns the stored snapshot via handleExisting.
Hashes the request body so a different body under the same key can be detected.

lookFor: The response's settlementId is identical. The account balance moved once. The step list is a single 'idempotency key already known' step.
honestLimit: The key table is the only dedup. A client that invents a new key for a retry is a new request.

title: Same key, different body
visitorSees: Re-using a key with a changed amount is rejected as a 409 conflict instead of being treated as a retry.

engineDoes.what: compares the stored request hash with the new one and throws IdempotencyKeyReusedException.

lookFor: httpStatus 409 in the envelope, and no new settlement row.
honestLimit: The hash covers accounts, amount and currency only.

title: A duplicate arrives mid-flight (409 in progress)
visitorSees: Start a settlement with a slow gateway, then send the same key again before it finishes. The second request is told the first is still running.

engineDoes.what: sees IN_PROGRESS and throws SettlementInProgressException (409).

lookFor: The second response is a 409 while the first is still waiting on the gateway.
honestLimit: The window is as long as the injected latency (at most 3 seconds). In production it is as long as the real gateway call.

title: Case 1: the request never reached the external system
visitorSees: The gateway throws before any external record is written. The settlement ends UNKNOWN with no reference.

engineDoes.what: catches the gateway exception and finalizes UNKNOWN with a null reference.
throws before delegating to the mock (a lost request).

lookFor: Status UNKNOWN, externalRef null, no external record held. It is flagged as stranded.
honestLimit: Nothing will ever resolve this settlement. Reconciliation only loads settlements that have a reference.

doc.label: Open questions: UNKNOWN with no externalRef

title: Case 2: the external system did it, the response was lost
visitorSees: The external system holds a record, but the engine never learned its reference. The settlement ends UNKNOWN with no reference.

engineDoes.what: delegates to MockExternalSystem (which writes the record) and then throws.
treats the exception as 'we do not know' and finalizes UNKNOWN.

lookFor: The playground shows the orphaned external reference. Money moved externally, not internally.
honestLimit: The engine cannot recover the reference. This is the case reconciliation was built for, and it still cannot reach it.

doc.label: Open questions: UNKNOWN with no externalRef

title: A definite decline
visitorSees: The gateway answers FAILED. The settlement is FAILED and no money moves.

engineDoes.what: writes FAILED, no ledger entries, a settlement.failed event.

lookFor: No ledger entries, balances unchanged. Driven at volume it pushes the SettlementFailureRateSpike alert.
honestLimit: A decline is the easy case: the engine is told the truth.

title: A slow gateway
visitorSees: The gateway answers correctly but late (up to 3 seconds). The latency shows in the request and in the trace.

engineDoes.what: sleeps, then delegates.

lookFor: The gateway span is the long one in the trace. A parallel duplicate gets a 409.
honestLimit: The call holds a request thread for the whole delay. There is no timeout in the engine's gateway call.

title: A crash between the two transactions
visitorSees: A settlement stays PENDING with its key IN_PROGRESS, exactly as after a hard crash. Retries get 409 until the sweep finalizes it.

engineDoes.what: commits the pending row and stops.
after the grace period, finalizes it as UNKNOWN and unblocks the key.

lookFor: PENDING, then UNKNOWN once the (compressed) grace period has passed. The idempotency key becomes COMPLETED.
honestLimit: This reproduces the database state of a crash. It does not kill a process.

doc.label: Recovering from a crash before finalization

title: The external record disappears
visitorSees: Forget an external record. After the grace period, reconciliation opens a 'No external record found' mismatch.

engineDoes.what: finds no record past the grace period and calls flagMismatch.

lookFor: An OPEN mismatch with the settlement id, plus a reconciliation.mismatch_found outbox event.
honestLimit: Nothing alerts a human. The mismatch is seen only if someone opens the reconciliation screen.

title: The external record disagrees
visitorSees: Change an external record's amount, currency or status. The next run opens a mismatch that names which one.

engineDoes.what: compares amount and currency, then status, and flags a mismatch; it never auto-resolves a CONFIRMED or FAILED settlement.

lookFor: Different details text for amount/currency versus status mismatches.
honestLimit: Resolving records a reason and an audit entry. It does not change the settlement or the balance.

title: Resolving a mismatch does not change data
visitorSees: Resolve a settlement or ledger mismatch with the real endpoint. The balance and the settlement are untouched.

engineDoes.what: records the reason, marks the row RESOLVED, audit-logs it.

lookFor: After resolving a ledger mismatch, the next read of the account opens a fresh row.
honestLimit: No endpoint corrects data. The Lab's repair helper is a stand-in for a human editing the database.

doc.label: Open questions: resolving does not correct data

title: Someone edits a balance by hand
visitorSees: A direct row update makes the stored balance disagree with its entries. Reading the account returns 500 and opens a ledger mismatch.

engineDoes.what: compares the stored balance with the net of its entries on every GET /accounts/{id}.
maps LedgerInconsistencyException to 500.

lookFor: 500 with both numbers, one OPEN ledger mismatch. Resolve it without repairing: the next read opens another.
honestLimit: Only accounts someone reads are ever checked. The repair button is a lab-only helper, not a product feature.

title: Stranded UNKNOWN settlements
visitorSees: A list of settlements stuck in UNKNOWN with no reference, and why reconciliation cannot touch them.

engineDoes.what: loads only findByExternalRefIsNotNull(), so these never enter a run.

lookFor: They stay UNKNOWN after any number of runs. No mismatch is ever opened for them.
honestLimit: Shown as it is. Fixing it is a separate decision.

doc.label: Open questions: UNKNOWN with no externalRef

title: REVERSED has no code path
visitorSees: One settlement is REVERSED, seeded by hand. The state machine allows CONFIRMED to REVERSED, but nothing transitions there.

engineDoes.what: allows CONFIRMED to REVERSED; no code in src/main calls it.

lookFor: The state machine on /lab marks REVERSED 'seeded by hand, no code path produces this'.
honestLimit: Reversals are not implemented.

title: Nobody is told about a mismatch
visitorSees: An 'Unseen mismatches' count that grows until someone opens the reconciliation screen, and a topic with zero consumers.

engineDoes.what: publishes reconciliation.mismatch_found through the outbox. Nothing consumes it.

lookFor: Consumers: 0 on reconciliation.mismatch_found. The alert board has a row for the rule that does not exist.
honestLimit: The unseen count is the Lab's measure, not a product feature.

title: A clean invoice
visitorSees: An established account, a unique customer reference and a modest advance. Score 0, ALLOW.

engineDoes.what: computes the fraud features, calls POST /score, stores a FraudAssessment, blocks or claims the invoice.
fails open when the service is unreachable.

lookFor: Score, decision and reasons exactly as the service returned them: No rule fires.
honestLimit: Rules are four hand-written thresholds, not a trained model.

title: A duplicate customer reference
visitorSees: The same reference already sits on another business's invoice. Score 0.4, still ALLOW.

engineDoes.what: computes the fraud features, calls POST /score, stores a FraudAssessment, blocks or claims the invoice.
fails open when the service is unreachable.

lookFor: Score, decision and reasons exactly as the service returned them: duplicate_customer_reference (+0.4)
honestLimit: One rule alone never blocks.

title: A new account with a high advance
visitorSees: A brand-new account asks for more than 500. Score 0.3, ALLOW.

engineDoes.what: computes the fraud features, calls POST /score, stores a FraudAssessment, blocks or claims the invoice.
fails open when the service is unreachable.

lookFor: Score, decision and reasons exactly as the service returned them: new_account_high_advance (+0.3)
honestLimit: Account age is computed from the ledger account's creation time.

title: Rapid refinancing
visitorSees: The account already has three outstanding advances. Score 0.3, ALLOW.

engineDoes.what: computes the fraud features, calls POST /score, stores a FraudAssessment, blocks or claims the invoice.
fails open when the service is unreachable.

lookFor: Score, decision and reasons exactly as the service returned them: rapid_refinancing (+0.3)
honestLimit: Counts FINANCED and OVERDUE invoices on the account.

title: The combination that blocks
visitorSees: Duplicate reference on a new account with a high advance reaches 0.7 and is BLOCKed. Nothing is disbursed.

engineDoes.what: computes the fraud features, calls POST /score, stores a FraudAssessment, blocks or claims the invoice.
fails open when the service is unreachable.

lookFor: Score, decision and reasons exactly as the service returned them: duplicate_customer_reference + new_account_high_advance = 0.7 (the BLOCK threshold)
honestLimit: If the ml-service is down the backend fails open and allows financing.

title: Mark an invoice paid, run repayment
visitorSees: Mark a financed invoice paid in the mock payment source, then run the repayment job. The business repays advance plus fee.

engineDoes.what: detects the payment, creates the repayment settlement, records the repayment.
records the payment in memory.

lookFor: Invoice REPAID, advance REPAID, a second settlement from business to platform. A wrong amount is left for review.
honestLimit: The payment source is in memory: a restart forgets it.

title: Fresh settlements across the pool
visitorSees: Several virtual users create settlements between six accounts. Live throughput, latency percentiles, outcomes and connection pool use.

engineDoes.what: sends real HTTP requests to this app on loopback with the sandbox ADMIN token.

lookFor: Invariants at the end: pool total unchanged, balances equal their entries, outbox drained, read model caught up.
honestLimit: Runs on the same host as the app, with a JVM client. Numbers differ from k6.

title: Duplicate-key burst
visitorSees: Many virtual users send the same Idempotency-Key at once. Money moves exactly once.

engineDoes.what: one request wins the key insert; the others get the cached result or a 409.

lookFor: The duplicate-key invariant: the pair moved by exactly one settlement's amount.
honestLimit: Under heavy contention Postgres deadlocks are retried and, if exhausted, fall back to UNKNOWN.

title: Load with injected faults
visitorSees: A load run where some calls lose their response or are declined. UNKNOWN outcomes appear as a count, not as a failure.

engineDoes.what: finalizes lost calls as UNKNOWN; the counters settlement.finalize.retries and settlement.unknown.fallback show contention.

lookFor: The stranded count with its explanation, and the invariants still passing.
honestLimit: Faults are injected at the gateway boundary only.

doc.label: Open questions: UNKNOWN with no externalRef

title: Take the fraud service down
visitorSees: For up to 60 seconds the ml-service answers 503. MLServiceDown goes pending then firing, and financing still works (fail open).

engineDoes.what: returns allowNoSignal on any client error.

lookFor: The alert board, the health strip, and a clean invoice still financing with no fraud signal.
honestLimit: The sandbox uses shorter for: durations than staging. The real durations are shown beside them.

title: Three roles, real 200s and 403s
visitorSees: Switch between ADMIN, SUPPORT and READ_ONLY and call the real endpoints. READ_ONLY sees only its own accounts.

engineDoes.what: filters by the owner id in the token.

lookFor: READ_ONLY reading someone else's inconsistent account gets 500, not 403: the ledger check runs before the ownership check.
honestLimit: That ordering is a recorded weakness in docs/security.md, shown as it is.

title: Events arriving out of order
visitorSees: A settlement.confirmed event published before its settlement.requested. The read model keeps the later state.

engineDoes.what: applies a last-write-wins check on the event timestamp.

lookFor: The read model row ends CONFIRMED whichever order the events arrive in.
honestLimit: Optional demo; uses the real producer on the real topics.
